clue.text: Nevertheless returned to cover separate social event

indicators.note: to cover means the turned-round word wraps around the next piece
returned means the word for nevertheless is read backwards

parts.note: nevertheless means yet, still
separate as an adverb, apart, set at a distance

explanation.surface: Despite everything, someone came back to oversee a separate social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the word for nevertheless, and 'to cover' wraps it around 'separate' used as an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon gathering where tea and cakes are served is a classic example of a social occasion.

clue.text: Pub having area for small restaurant

parts.note: a tavern is an inn or pub

explanation.surface: An inn with some extra space serves as a little eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek eating house, usually modest in size, is a small restaurant.

clue.text: Missile, not wide, with top missing

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: something not wide is narrow

explanation.surface: A projectile that is slim and has lost its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with top missing' takes the N off NARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft shot from a bow is a missile, an object propelled at a target.

clue.text: Moan — all do it when off drink

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Everyone grumbles when their beverage has gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals rearranging MOAN ALL DO IT; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-dry Spanish sherry is a fortified wine, hence a drink.

clue.text: Sailor needing to achieve objective

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to get something is to obtain or achieve it

explanation.surface: A seaman must reach his goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is the goal or aim one sets out to reach, a synonym of objective.

clue.text: Friendly with member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: Someone sociable who belongs to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a friendly, cordial one, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: One failing to gain a place in final — so rancorous

definitions.text: One failing to gain a place

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A runner unplaced in the final is bitter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fin-AL SO RAN-corous.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse finishing out of the first three is an also-ran, hence any loser.

clue.text: Minutes before oral, damaged back tooth

indicators.note: damaged means the following word is knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Shortly before an oral exam, a rear tooth gets injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' is the anagram signal, acting on 'oral', which in the surface reads as an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinding tooth at the back of the mouth is one of these.

clue.text: Ill-tempered woman ignoring a sign

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter given by a is left out

parts.note: a virago is a domineering, bad-tempered woman

explanation.surface: A grumpy woman disregards a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Initially find American to be in genuine denial

indicators.note: to be in means these pieces go inside the word for genuine

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of find is taken

explanation.surface: First discover that an American really is in a state of denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to a request is a refusal, a denial of what is asked.

clue.text: Popular tale about quiet Hebridean island

indicators.note: about means the story word goes round the rest

parts.note: a fable is a short moral tale
sh is the call for quiet
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A well-loved story concerns a peaceful Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the story goes round the rest, not that the tale concerns the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is widely liked and current, so popular in that sense.

clue.text: Argument in bank

definitions.meaning: a line or tier, as of seats or keys

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a quarrel (rhyming with cow) and a line of things (rhyming with low).

clue.text: Club official, person much valued at end of year

parts.note: a treasure is a much-loved, valued person

indicators.note: at end of means the final letter of year is taken

explanation.surface: A society's officer is a gem of a person by the year's close.
explanation.definitionFit: The member who keeps the accounts is one of a club's elected officers.

clue.text: A grand on top

parts.note: swell, chiefly American, means grand or excellent

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds placed on the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds, but it is the adjective, splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: On top in the sense of in addition or besides, an idiom for also.

clue.text: Wodehouse character in court, unsmiling mostly

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: unsmiling means stern

explanation.surface: A P G Wodehouse figure stands in a court room, barely cracking a smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims STERN to STER; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie, the hapless young man served by Jeeves, is P G Wodehouse's best-known creation.

clue.text: Like Steve Austin on island cornered by writer

indicators.note: cornered by means the pen brand surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A TV hero's island refuge, trapped by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is not an author but a pen: Bic is a ballpoint brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Austin, the Six Million Dollar Man of 1970s television, had robotic body parts.

clue.text: Irish girl in place of learning lacking good name

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a college is a place of learning

explanation.surface: An Irish girl at university who has no reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: From Irish cailín, the word for a girl or young woman in Ireland.

clue.text: Petty quarrel at home making ex-pat's light midday meal

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
in means at home

explanation.surface: A squabble at home over a lunch abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: In British India, Anglo-Indian usage gave the name to a light lunch or snack.

clue.text: A speech about daughter's deep love

indicators.note: about means the words A and speech surround the next piece

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speech about one's daughter expresses profound affection.
explanation.walkthrough: A and ORATION go round D; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship or devoted admiration is profound love.

clue.text: Permit inexperienced leader to drop out

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: callow means young and inexperienced

explanation.surface: Let a novice captain quit the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to let it happen, which is to give leave for it.

clue.text: Everybody in a large lake

explanation.surface: Everyone is in a big lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole group, every single person, is the sense of everybody.

clue.text: Reference book sadly includes typos at the start

indicators.note: includes means the word for sadly holds the next letter

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of typos is taken

explanation.surface: Unfortunately the reference work has misprints from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps is a standard reference work.

clue.text: Excuses made by the Parisian to fine female carrying son

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: carrying means the preceding letters hold the one for son

parts.note: F is short for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Frenchman makes excuses to fine a woman who has her son with her.
explanation.walkthrough: S sits inside TOFF; 'made by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone a penalty is to let them escape it, a verb phrase meaning pardons.

clue.text: Rubbish can be left in large receptacle at the end

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for large

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: at the end means the last letter of receptacle is taken

explanation.surface: Waste may be dumped in a big bin at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a container, but 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or worthless talk is rubbish, named after dirty water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Cautious fighting by Dempsey, ultimately

parts.note: war is fighting between nations

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of Dempsey is taken

explanation.surface: Jack Dempsey, the boxer, was careful in the ring at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's guard against danger is the sense shared by cautious.

clue.text: Elected to add flavouring available

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
to season food is to add flavouring

explanation.surface: A newly elected member chooses to add spice to things.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or game that is obtainable at the right time of year is available.
